candidates.particulars: Philip Grant Holladay is a 78-year-old American man, White and non-Hispanic, living in Colorado. He is married to Anne; they have no children. Their gross household income is about $240,000 a year, from retirement income, investments, and Anne’s occasional consulting. He identifies as moderately conservative: he values personal responsibility and continuity, is wary of expansive government, and accepts public programs such as Medicare. He enjoys reading, especially astronomy writing, science history, and biographies.
candidates.life_course: Philip spent most of his career as an electrical engineer, eventually managing technical teams. The work suited his habit of asking how things function, though he preferred practical problem-solving to office politics. He and Anne have been married for decades and built a comfortable life without children, with savings that let them retire without giving up their interests. He still likes having a project to anticipate, but does not miss the demands of full-time work.
candidates.daily_life: His favorite free time is stargazing with Anne and, occasionally, a small local astronomy group. He maintains his telescope, checks the sky forecast, and enjoys learning to identify objects rather than treating the hobby as a checklist. Anne is more interested in the shared quiet than in the technical details, and they often talk afterward over coffee. He also reads science books and keeps notes on what he has observed.
candidates.travel: Philip travels to experience genuinely dark skies and the sense of scale he gets from watching the night sky away from city lights. A past trip to a high-desert area, where he carried his telescope out after dinner and stayed up to watch a meteor shower, convinced him that a few clear nights can make a trip memorable. He would also enjoy visiting an observatory or joining a small astronomy gathering. He and Anne usually drive, bring the telescope and binoculars, and choose a comfortable, quiet place to stay with several nights available in case clouds interrupt the plan. They leave daytime activities loose rather than packing every hour.
candidates.personality_and_voice: He is curious, dryly funny, and happiest when someone asks a precise question. He can get absorbed in technical explanations and miss a hint that the group is ready to move on. With friends, he is a patient listener until a claim sounds sloppy; then he asks, mildly but firmly, what the evidence is.

candidates.particulars: Philip Grant Holladay is an 83-year-old American man, White and non-Hispanic, living in Montana. He is married to Ruth, and they have no children. Their gross household income is approximately $225,000 annually, largely from retirement income and investments accumulated over a long career. He describes himself as moderately conservative, emphasizing self-reliance and tradition while supporting public programs he considers useful. He reads for pleasure, particularly engineering histories, biographies, and books about vintage automobiles.
candidates.life_course: Philip worked as a mechanical engineer and later ran a small consulting firm, where he enjoyed solving design problems more than managing people. He sold the business before retiring and has enough financial flexibility to pursue a long-standing interest in restoring cars. Ruth shares his fondness for travel and old buildings, though she has never cared much about engines. Their child-free household has given them room for a workshop and for hobbies that take up both space and time.
candidates.daily_life: What Philip most wants to do is work on his restored early-1960s sports car and spend time with other people who know the difference between a thoughtful repair and a quick cosmetic fix. He keeps a modest workshop, trades advice with a few local enthusiasts, and goes to regional car gatherings. A good day includes solving one stubborn mechanical problem, then telling Ruth about it over dinner. He reads technical manuals alongside memoirs and automotive histories.
candidates.travel: His trips are motivated by seeing how car design and repair traditions differ from place to place, and by meeting craftspeople who have kept old machines running. On a past trip, he and Ruth visited an automobile collection and took a scenic drive through smaller towns; he remembers the conversations with volunteer mechanics as much as the cars. He would like another trip built around a specialist gathering, a museum visit, and a route worth driving. They travel in their newer vehicle, plan one or two main stops, and choose lodging with easy parking. If taking his restored car, he would arrange transport rather than risk a long journey in it.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Philip is direct, competitive in a friendly way, and quick to tease someone who makes an overconfident claim about a car. He enjoys swapping stories but can dominate a conversation when a repair topic comes up. Ruth knows when to interrupt him with a question about the trip itself.

candidates.particulars: Philip Grant Holladay is a 76-year-old American man, White and non-Hispanic, living in Idaho. He is married to Marjorie; they have no children. Their gross household income is around $235,000 a year, supported by retirement income and investments after a successful small food business. Philip is moderately conservative, favoring personal responsibility and familiar institutions while recognizing a role for public programs. He reads for pleasure, especially cookbooks, food memoirs, and books about the history of everyday life.
candidates.life_course: Philip began his working life in accounting, then joined Marjorie in building a specialty food business. He handled budgets and suppliers while becoming increasingly interested in the people and traditions behind the products they sold. They sold the business before retirement and kept enough resources to be comfortable without needing to turn every hobby into an enterprise. Their long marriage is companionable, though Marjorie is more organized than Philip about making plans.
candidates.daily_life: In his free time Philip likes cooking an unfamiliar dish for Marjorie and a few friends, then lingering at the table to ask what people noticed. He experiments with recipes, visits local food shops, and reads cookbooks as much for their stories as their instructions. He is less interested in perfect presentation than in whether the flavors make sense. He and Marjorie often host informal meals, where conversation matters as much as the menu.
candidates.travel: He travels to encounter regional food traditions in context: what people grow, how migration shaped a cuisine, and what a dish means to the cooks who make it. A past trip to New Mexico was especially satisfying because they tried home-style regional cooking, talked with shopkeepers, and came back with ideas Philip adapted for dinner parties. He would like future trips to include a market or cooking demonstration as well as meals at restaurants, not just a string of reservations. He and Marjorie generally fly when the distance warrants it, rent a car for smaller towns, and reserve a few anchor activities while leaving room to follow a recommendation. They prefer comfortable lodging with a usable kitchen, since Philip likes to recreate a dish after returning.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Philip is sociable, opinionated, and apt to turn a casual meal into a lively discussion about whether a recipe has been improved or merely modernized. He likes welcoming newcomers and remembers what people enjoy eating. If he thinks a dish is overpraised, he says so plainly, then asks for another helping.

candidates.particulars: Philip Grant Holladay is a 80-year-old American man, White and non-Hispanic, living in Wyoming. He is married to Ellen, and they have no children. Their gross household income is about $210,000 per year, combining retirement benefits and investment income. He is moderately conservative, valuing independence, tradition, and limited government while accepting public programs that provide practical support. He enjoys reading, especially natural history, field guides, and personal accounts of wildlife observation.
candidates.life_course: Philip spent his career as a physician, a demanding job that rewarded careful observation. He retired gradually and now appreciates having mornings that are not scheduled around patients. Ellen, also retired, enjoys being outdoors but is content to let Philip choose the route and keep the sightings list. Their finances are comfortable, though they still pay attention to healthcare and home-maintenance costs. They have no children and have shaped retirement around shared outings and independent interests.
candidates.daily_life: Philip most wants to spend his free time watching birds, often with Ellen on an early walk and sometimes with a local conservation-minded group. He keeps binoculars and a notebook ready, takes photographs when the light allows, and enjoys learning how behavior changes with season and habitat. He sometimes helps record observations for local projects, but does not want every outing to feel like work. In the afternoon he reads field guides or natural-history writing and compares notes with fellow birders.
candidates.travel: His reason for traveling is to witness migration and unfamiliar bird habitats, not simply to collect destinations. A past trip to Gulf Coast wetlands during migration gave him the pleasure of seeing species he knew from books in a living landscape; he still recalls the changing light and the conversations with other observers. He hopes to make another trip focused on marshes or coastal birdlife, with time to watch rather than rush between stops. He and Ellen plan around the season and likely habitat, bring binoculars and a camera, and may arrange a local guide for one outing while keeping other mornings open. They prefer a quiet, comfortable base and a rental car, with shorter walks and time to rest between field days.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Philip is reserved in a large group and dislikes being hurried through an observation. Among birders he becomes animated, asks pointed questions, and remembers small details others miss. His humor is understated; he is more likely to make one dry remark than to fill a silence.
